title: Coupled statistical and deep-learning models link teleconnection indices with Yalong River runoff forecasts
summary: Using monthly runoff records from four Yalong River Basin stations for 1953–2011 and atmospheric-circulation indices, the study reports a one-month index lag as most informative and identifies Northern Hemisphere Polar Vortex and East Asian Trough indices among predictive variables. SRA-MLPR reduced reported RMSE from 798.47 to 594.45 and MAPE from 34.79% to 22.90% versus the stated baseline, with NSE increasing from 0.67 to 0.76. The held-out data come from the same basin and time-series source; these predictive associations do not establish causal climate effects or transfer to other basins.
ai_technology: Stepwise regression, support vector regression, multilayer perceptron regression, and SHAP analysis

evidence.tested: Coupled models were evaluated on a held-out subset of four-station historical runoff data; the article reports 10-fold cross-validation and compares forecast metrics with baseline models.
evidence.unknown: The evaluation uses a single basin and historical time series; external basin transfer and causal climate attribution are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Stepwise regression selected atmospheric-index features and SVR/MLP models forecast runoff; SHAP was used to rank model predictors.

source_review.scope: Full primary publisher article and primary bibliographic metadata, including Methods, Results, author affiliations and publication history
